blocks.text: The International Court of Justice (ICJ) will deliver on Thursday its long-awaited judgment in The Gambia’s landmark genocide case against Myanmar, seven years after the case was lodged in The Hague. The Gambia filed the case with the United Nations’ top court in November 2019, formally accusing the Southeast Asian nation of breaking its obligations under the 1948 UN Genocide Convention. In documents and hearings, The Gambia has alleged that Myanmar waged a deliberate campaign of arson, rape and murder in Rakhine State from 2016 to 2017, intending to wipe out the area’s ethnic Rohingya minority, in whole or in part.
